title: Clever Molly May
year_evidence: 扉に『PUBLISHED BY THE AMERICAN FOLK-LORE SOCIETY … 1924』、序文の署名に『April, 1924.』
text:
Emily Alexander, Mandeville.

Once Anansi went out to invite a friend to dinner. Little Molly May was
his servant, so he left her to roast a turkey for dinner. Anansi filled
the wine-jug, laid the table, put on his frock coat and his top hat,
took his walking-stick and went out for his friend. Molly May roasted
the turkey. Seeing that it looked so nice and charming, she thought
that she would take a piece; so she did, and it tasted so nice she took
another piece. That tasted so nice she took a next piece and a sip of
the wine, and she sipped and tasted till at last she had eaten up the
whole turkey and drunk the whole of the wine.

She saw the master coming; so she ran in swift haste, took up the
bones, fixed them nicely in the dish, covered the dish, and carried it
and laid it on the table. When the master came, he sent the visitor
into the house and said to Molly May, “Hullo, deh! everyt’ing all
right?” She said, “Yes, sah! all is right.” So the master took up the
carving-knife and went outside to sharpen it. Molly ran inside and told
the visitor that the master was sharpening the knife to cut off one of
his hands; the visitor in swift haste left the house. Then Molly went
outside and told the master that the visitor had eaten all the turkey
and drunk the wine. The master ran through one door and, seeing all the
bones on the table, went through the other. The visitor was running for
his life and Anansi went running after him, calling “Leave one! leave
one!” He meant leave one (side of) the turkey, but the visitor thought
he meant one of his hands, so he ran for his life.
paragraphs: Once Anansi went out to invite a friend to dinner. Little Molly May was his servant, so he left her to roast a turkey for dinner. Anansi filled the wine-jug, laid the table, put on his frock coat and his top hat, took his walking-stick and went out for his friend. Molly May roasted the turkey. Seeing that it looked so nice and charming, she thought that she would take a piece; so she did, and it tasted so nice she took another piece. That tasted so nice she took a next piece and a sip of the wine, and she sipped and tasted till at last she had eaten up the whole turkey and drunk the whole of the wine.

She saw the master coming; so she ran in swift haste, took up the bones, fixed them nicely in the dish, covered the dish, and carried it and laid it on the table. When the master came, he sent the visitor into the house and said to Molly May, “Hullo, deh! everyt’ing all right?” She said, “Yes, sah! all is right.” So the master took up the carving-knife and went outside to sharpen it. Molly ran inside and told the visitor that the master was sharpening the knife to cut off one of his hands; the visitor in swift haste left the house. Then Molly went outside and told the master that the visitor had eaten all the turkey and drunk the wine. The master ran through one door and, seeing all the bones on the table, went through the other. The visitor was running for his life and Anansi went running after him, calling “Leave one! leave one!” He meant leave one (side of) the turkey, but the visitor thought he meant one of his hands, so he ran for his life.
語り手 エミリー・アレグザンダー(マンデヴィル)

あるときアナンシが友を夕食に招きに出かけた。小さなモリー・メイが召使いだったので、夕食の七面鳥を焼いておくように言いつけて出かけた。アナンシは葡萄酒の水差しを満たし、食卓をととのえ、フロックコートを着て山高帽をかぶり、杖を持って友を迎えに出た。モリー・メイは七面鳥を焼いた。それがあまりにおいしそうで見事なので、ひと切れいただこうと思った。そうしてみるとあまりにおいしいので、もうひと切れ取った。それもあまりにおいしいのでもうひと切れ取り、葡萄酒もひと口すすった。そうしてすすり、味わっているうちに、とうとう七面鳥を丸ごと食べ、葡萄酒を残らず飲んでしまった。

主人が帰ってくるのが見えた。そこで大急ぎで駆け込んで骨を拾い上げ、きれいに皿に並べ、蓋をして、食卓に運んで置いた。主人が帰ってくると、客を家へ通してモリー・メイに言った。「おおい! 何もかも大丈夫か?」 モリーは「はい旦那さま、何もかも大丈夫です」と言った。そこで主人は肉切り包丁を取り、外へ研ぎに出た。モリーは家のなかへ駆け込んで客に、旦那さまはあなたの手を片方切り落とすために包丁を研いでいるのだと告げた。客は大急ぎで家を出ていった。それからモリーは外へ出て主人に、お客さまが七面鳥をみんな食べて葡萄酒も飲んでしまったと告げた。主人は一方の戸から駆け込み、食卓の骨をみな見て、もう一方の戸から駆け出した。客は命からがら逃げ、アナンシはそのあとを追いかけながら叫んだ。「一つ残せ! 一つ残せ!」 アナンシは七面鳥の(片身を)一つ残せと言ったつもりだったが、客は手を片方残せと言われたと思って、命がけで逃げていった。
